principles: Candidate, diagnostic, legacy, local-key, Authority receipt, and production gate decision must remain mechanically distinct.
This slice is warn/classification-only; enforcement follows later stories.
Reason codes must be stable enough for operators, reviewers, and future gates.
drivers: Reduce repeated proof-surface bugs across metadata, receipts, handoff, and local diagnostics.
Provide a reusable M1 contract for later M2-M7 hardening slices.
Give users a visible command/test that proves classification behavior.

options.name: A: registry/classifier MVP only
pros: Small enough to complete safely in one story
Establishes shared enums, surface definitions, and reason codes for future gates
Does not break existing DONE/Authority/local workflows
cons: Does not yet enforce reserved-key stripping or hard-fail inadmissible gate evidence

options.name: B: full enforce-mode rollout now
pros: Would address more plan milestones in one pass
Could immediately block more spoofing surfaces
cons: Too risky because it touches REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority/handoff gates at once
Likely causes false blocks without legacy migration and warning period

options.name: C: documentation-only inventory
cons: Does not give callers a machine-readable classifier or stable reason codes
Would not satisfy the user request to develop the feature

rationale: Choose A because M0/M1 are explicit blockers for the rest of the plan. A creates the shared contract, inventory, and smoke-tested classification behavior while preserving current gate behavior until warn/enforce integration is developed separately.

preMortem.scenario: A future gate treats authority-receipt as productionDone by reading only the scope label.
preMortem.trigger: Registry naming is ambiguous or claim evaluation collapses receipt evidence and gate decision.
preMortem.consequence: Local or partial Authority evidence could be overclaimed as production completion.
preMortem.mitigation: Encode authority-receipt and production-gate-decision as distinct scopes and add smoke tests denying production claim for receipt-only inputs.

preMortem.scenario: The classifier becomes another parallel proof implementation instead of the shared contract.
preMortem.trigger: Definitions are hard-coded in one task or handler and not reusable by future gate integration.
preMortem.consequence: M2-M7 stories fork logic again and the original problem persists.
preMortem.mitigation: Put domain types and registry in core/proof-admissibility.ts and register a process fact for the smoke/command path.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy or candidate evidence gets mislabeled as strong proof.
preMortem.trigger: Default behavior accepts missing fields as admissible to avoid breaking old data.
preMortem.consequence: Old or pre-story evidence can satisfy claims it should only inform.
preMortem.mitigation: Fail closed for missing definitions and unsupported scope/claim combinations; classify legacy/candidate/local diagnostic as non-production by default.

preMortem.scenario: The feature passes tests but users cannot see useful output.
preMortem.trigger: Smoke only asserts internal booleans and does not expose reason codes or inventory shape.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer/product advisory remains unresolved and operators still need manual interpretation.
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke tests assert stable reason codes and inventory artifacts document producer, scope, consumers, and claim boundaries.
